wiki_catalogs.name: Project Overview
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for the FractalDharma project overview section. Explain its purpose as a Sanskrit text exploration platform that creates an interconnected web of Dharmic texts through linguistic analysis. Document the three primary pathways: textual reading, verbal root (dhātu) analysis, and semantic concept mapping. Describe the technical architecture built with SvelteKit, the target audience including researchers and students of Sanskrit literature, and key features like the interactive word lens, graph visualization, and multi-script display. Include both conceptual overviews for beginners unfamiliar with digital humanities tools and technical details for developers. Use terminology consistent with the codebase such as 'lemmas', 'supersenses', and 'artifacts'. Provide practical examples demonstrating the research workflows and explain how this platform bridges traditional Sanskrit scholarship with modern web technologies.

wiki_catalogs.name: Explorer API
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive API documentation for the Explorer endpoint. Document the GET /api/explorer endpoint with two query modes: root-based exploration and word-based exploration. For root queries, explain the 'root' parameter, response structure with nodes containing id, label, type ('root' | 'word' | 'text'), weight, and count fields. For word queries, detail the 'word' parameter, response format including lemma details, English definitions, root information (slug, meaning, grammatical classification), concept mappings, sibling words, and text distribution data. Include request/response examples, error handling patterns, and integration guidelines for building exploration interfaces.

wiki_catalogs.name: Architecture Overview
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive architectural documentation for FractalDharma's SvelteKit-based system. Detail the runtime stack including Svelte 5 with runes mode, TypeScript strict mode, Dart Sass styling, and Vercel deployment. Explain the rendering model with SSR/CSR behavior, static-data application design, and versioned JSON data architecture. Document the shared navigation state management using reactive stores, component composition patterns, and the separation between build-time assets and runtime artifacts. Include system boundaries, technology decisions, and architectural constraints. Provide diagrams showing component interactions, data flow patterns, and deployment topology. Address performance considerations, scalability factors, and the rationale behind key architectural choices.

Address coverage limitations and explain how missing information indicates evolving data rather than unimportant content.

wiki_overview.content:
<blog>

# FractalDharma: A Comprehensive Sanskrit Text Exploration Platform

## Project Introduction

FractalDharma is a sophisticated digital humanities platform designed to create an interconnected web of Dharmic texts through Sanskrit linguistic analysis. The project serves as a near-comprehensive, indexed, searchable, and AI-ready repository of Dharmic texts, enabling deep exploration of Sanskrit literature through three primary pathways: textual reading, verbal root (dhātu) analysis, and semantic concept mapping.

### Purpose Statement
The platform aims to facilitate "synaptic reconnection with the Indian civilizational consciousness" by creating interlinked Sanskritic networks that enable discovery and exploration across multiple dimensions of Sanskrit scholarship.

### Core Goals
- **Textual Accessibility**: Provide structured access to classical Sanskrit texts with verse-by-verse navigation
- **Linguistic Analysis**: Enable deep grammatical and morphological analysis through dhātu (verbal root) exploration
- **Semantic Navigation**: Connect concepts through supersenses and synsets linking lemmas by semantic relationships
- **Research Support**: Offer tools for scholars and students to explore Sanskrit literature systematically

### Target Audience
- Sanskrit scholars and researchers
- Students of Indian philosophy and literature
- Linguists studying Indo-Aryan languages
- Digital humanities practitioners
- Cultural heritage enthusiasts

## Technical Architecture

The project follows a modern SvelteKit architecture with a clear separation between frontend components, data management, and build-time artifact generation.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Client[Client Browser] --> Router[SvelteKit Router]
    Router --> Layout[App Layout]
    Router --> Pages[Route Pages]
    
    Layout --> LeftPanel[Left Panel - Text Navigator]
    Layout --> MainPanel[Main Content Area]
    Layout --> RightPanel[Right Panel - Context Lens]
    
    Pages --> TextReader[Text Reader Component]
    Pages --> RootExplorer[Root Explorer]
    Pages --> ConceptExplorer[Concept Explorer]
    
    TextReader --> ContextLens[Context Lens]
    RootExplorer --> ContextLens
    ConceptExplorer --> ContextLens
    
    ContextLens --> DataClient[Data Client]
    DataClient --> Artifacts[Static Artifacts]
    DataClient --> API[API Routes]
    
    Artifacts --> GeneratedData[Generated JSON Artifacts]
    API --> ServerLogic[Server-side Processing]
```

### Component Breakdown

**Core Framework Layer:**
- **SvelteKit 2.x**: Modern full-stack framework with file-based routing
- **Svelte 5**: Reactive UI framework with runes for state management
- **Vite 8**: Fast build tool and development server

**UI Architecture:**
- **Three-panel layout**: Left navigation, main content, right context lens
- **Responsive design**: Mobile-first approach with adaptive layouts
- **Theme system**: Light/dark mode support with CSS custom properties

**Data Management:**
- **Artifact-based caching**: Pre-generated JSON artifacts for optimal performance
- **Request caching**: In-memory caching layer for repeated data access
- **Type-safe interfaces**: TypeScript definitions for all data structures

### Design Patterns

**Component Composition Pattern:**
```mermaid
classDiagram
    class AppLayout {
        +leftPanel()
        +mainPanel()
        +rightPanel()
        +PaneGroup
    }
    
    class TextReader {
        +verses: Verse[]
        +script: string
        +handleWordClick()
    }
    
    class ContextLens {
        +activeWord: ActiveWord
        +lemmaDetail: LemmaDetailArtifact
        +fetchLemmaData()
    }
    
    class NavigationStore {
        +activeView: View
        +navigatorMode: string
        +setActiveWord()
        +navigateTo()
    }
    
    AppLayout --> TextReader
    AppLayout --> ContextLens
    TextReader --> NavigationStore
    ContextLens --> NavigationStore
```

**State Management Pattern:**
The application uses Svelte's reactive stores pattern with the `navigation.svelte.ts` store managing global state including active views, breadcrumbs, pane visibility, and word selection.

## Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points
- **Application Shell**: `src/app.html` - HTML template with SvelteKit integration
- **Global Layout**: `src/routes/+layout.svelte` - Three-panel responsive layout with navigation
- **Home Page**: `src/routes/+page.svelte` - Landing page with three exploration pathways

### Core Modules

**Data Layer (`src/lib/data/`):**
- **Artifacts System**: `artifacts.ts` - Versioned artifact path generation and bucketing
- **Client Library**: `client.ts` - Cached fetch wrapper for artifact retrieval
- **Type Definitions**: `types.ts` - TypeScript interfaces for all data structures

**Component System (`src/lib/components/`):**
- **Text Reader**: `text-reader.svelte` - Dual-script verse display with interactive word highlighting
- **Context Lens**: `context-lens.svelte` - Dynamic sidebar showing lexical information for selected words
- **Navigation Components**: Various helper components for text browsing and filtering

**State Management (`src/lib/stores/`):**
- **Navigation Store**: `navigation.svelte.ts` - Centralized state for app-wide navigation and selection

### Configuration Approach
- **Build Configuration**: `svelte.config.js` - SvelteKit setup with mdsvex preprocessing and Vercel adapter
- **Package Management**: `package.json` - Dependencies managed via pnpm with strict version pinning
- **Development Scripts**: Comprehensive build pipeline for data processing and artifact generation

### External Dependencies
- **Visualization Libraries**: D3.js ecosystem for graph visualization and interaction
- **Layout Components**: Paneforge for resizable panel layouts
- **Animation**: svelte-animated-icon for smooth icon transitions
- **Language Processing**: sanscript for Sanskrit text normalization

### Integration Points
- **API Routes**: RESTful endpoints for search, graph queries, and text extraction
- **Static Asset Pipeline**: Build scripts for processing and optimizing large datasets
- **Content Management**: Markdown-based documentation with mdsvex preprocessing

## Key Features

### Functionality Overview

**Text Reading Experience:**
- Multi-script display (Devanāgarī, IAST, or both)
- Verse-by-verse navigation with pagination
- Interactive word highlighting and analysis
- Translation support with contextual tooltips

**Linguistic Analysis:**
- Real-time grammatical parsing with UPOS tagging
- Morphological feature display (case, gender, number, tense, etc.)
- Compound word decomposition and component analysis
- Cross-referencing with dictionary entries

**Exploration Pathways:**
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Home
    Home --> Texts: Click Texts
    Home --> Roots: Click Dhātus  
    Home --> Concepts: Click Concepts
    
    Texts --> TextReader: Select Text
    TextReader --> WordAnalysis: Click Word
    WordAnalysis --> DictionaryEntry: View Details
    DictionaryEntry --> RootPage: Follow Root
    RootPage --> WordGroups: Explore Derivations
    
    Roots --> RootExplorer: Select Root
    RootExplorer --> WordGroups: View Word Groups
    WordGroups --> LemmaDetails: Click Word
    LemmaDetails --> DictionaryEntry: View Details
    
    Concepts --> ConceptGraph: Select Concept
    ConceptGraph --> RelatedConcepts: Navigate Links
    RelatedConcepts --> DictionaryEntry: View Details
```

### Implementation Highlights

**Performance Optimization:**
- Static artifact generation at build time
- Intelligent request caching with deduplication
- Lazy loading of heavy data structures
- Efficient pagination for large text collections

**User Experience Features:**
- Responsive mobile layout with collapsible panels
- Keyboard navigation support
- Search functionality with fuzzy matching
- Breadcrumb navigation and history tracking

**Data Processing Pipeline:**
- Automated text splitting and indexing
- Lexical analysis and concordance generation
- Graph construction for concept relationships
- Artifact optimization and compression

### Feature Architecture

**Search and Discovery:**
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    UserInput[User Search Query] --> Normalizer[Text Normalization]
    Normalizer --> IndexLookup[Artifact Index Lookup]
    IndexLookup --> ResultFilter[Result Filtering]
    ResultFilter --> Display[Results Display]
    
    Display --> TextSelection[Text Selection]
    Display --> RootSelection[Root Selection]
    Display --> ConceptSelection[Concept Selection]
    
    TextSelection --> TextReader
    RootSelection --> RootExplorer
    ConceptSelection --> ConceptExplorer
```

**Interactive Word Analysis:**
The system provides real-time grammatical analysis when users click on words in texts, displaying part-of-speech tags, morphological features, and cross-references to dictionary entries and related textual occurrences.

**Multi-modal Navigation:**
Users can navigate through the corpus using three complementary approaches: textual reading for linear exploration, dhātu analysis for linguistic study, and concept mapping for thematic research.

---

**Sources:**
- [package.json](package.json)
- [svelte.config.js](svelte.config.js)
- [app.html](src/app.html)
- [+page.svelte](src/routes/+page.svelte)
- [+layout.svelte](src/routes/+layout.svelte)
- [hooks.server.ts](src/hooks.server.ts)
- [navigation.svelte.ts](src/lib/stores/navigation.svelte.ts)
- [types.ts](src/lib/data/types.ts)
- [+page.svelte](src/routes/text/[slug]/+page.svelte)
- [+page.ts](src/routes/text/[slug]/+page.ts)
- [client.ts](src/lib/data/client.ts)
- [artifacts.ts](src/lib/data/artifacts.ts)
- [text-reader.svelte](src/lib/components/text-reader.svelte)
- [context-lens.svelte](src/lib/components/context-lens.svelte)

</blog>
